question: Does the preceding pass add useful information for forecasting a deep throw beyond player history and release position?

source.freshness: Original exported rows; matching live counts do not establish current row identity.

method.unit: A located, non-stall pass by a named thrower, released at Y20 <= Y < 60 in a regular-season game.
method.target: Huck = receiverY - throwerY > 30 and Euclidean endpoint distance > 40 yards; outcomes include incomplete throws.
method.link: Same game, team side, quarter, point and possession; consecutive unique throw orders; unique increasing event sequences; prior completed non-stall pass with receiver equal to current thrower.
method.incomingDirection: forward: dy > abs(dx); backward: -dy > abs(dx); lateral otherwise for a finite nonzero prior vector. Missing/zero or unverifiable setups stay unclassified.
method.primaryComparison: direction vs availability on 2026 events, trained only on 2021–2025.
method.eligibility: At least 40 prior hucks in Y20–60, defined from historical labels only; 10-huck sensitivity.
method.penalties: Fixed L2 log-odds penalties: player 2.5; player-by-incoming interaction 5; other categorical features 1; intercept unpenalized.
method.selection: Primary comparison, seasons, models, thresholds and sensitivities fixed in the script before viewing the new result. Previously inspected 2026 makes this exploratory.
method.uncertainty: 5000 paired bootstrap draws of whole games and separately whole players. Conditional on fitted training models; neither interval captures all crossed dependence or model-selection uncertainty.
method.positiveImprovement: Lower Brier error. Relative reduction is loss difference divided by baseline loss; it is not a change in completion percentage.
method.topFifth: Rank all held-out passes by predicted huck probability with stable ID tie-break, select ceil(20% of passes). Descriptive ranking check, not a deployed coaching threshold.
limitations: Directions describe disc movement, not upline/swing cutting routes or dead-disc state.
No receiver positioning at release, mark, pressure, wind or stall count.
Release coordinates are current throw origins; a forecast made at the instant of catching may have different information.
Only recorded next throws are outcomes: catches with no subsequent recorded throw are outside this denominator.
Regular seasons and returning high-volume huckers only in the primary cohort; no causal defensive claim.
Temporal checks share training years and players, so they are not independent replications.
